summary: Describes the URLAUTH extension to IMAP, which lets a client use URLs carrying authorization to get limited message data from an IMAP server. A server shows support with the capability name URLAUTH. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: URLAUTH lets an IMAP user create a link to specific message data without giving the recipient access to the whole mailbox. The link can limit who may use it and when it expires.

questions: how do authorized imap urls work
what is the imap genurlauth command
how to revoke an imap url
subtitle: IMAP URLs can grant carefully limited access to a specific message or message part.

tldr.problem: An ordinary IMAP URL identifies a user as well as a mailbox location, so it normally requires logging in as that user and cannot grant limited access to one item.
tldr.mechanism: URLAUTH appends an access rule, mechanism, and token generated with a secret per-mailbox key. RESETKEY revokes URLs, GENURLAUTH creates them, and URLFETCH retrieves the addressed data.
tldr.outcome: A URL can be restricted to a particular user or role, made public, or given an expiry time. RFC 4467 is a Proposed Standard updated by RFC 5092 and RFC 5550.

today: RFC 4467 is a Proposed Standard published in May 2006. It updates RFC 3501 and has been updated by RFC 5092 and RFC 5550; it has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Why IMAP URLs Need Authorization
sections.content:
An ordinary IMAP URL identifies a mailbox and message, but its user component also implies that the user must log in. RFC 4467 separates authorization from authentication: the URL itself can grant access to the data it names, without granting access to other mailbox content.

A server that supports the extension advertises the URLAUTH capability. The URL can be used by a message submission service, such as for forwarding a message without first downloading it to the client.
sections.plainLanguage: Normally, an IMAP client must log in as the mailbox owner to open a URL. URLAUTH lets a user grant access to one addressed item without sharing the mailbox login.

sections.title: The Secret Key and Authorization Token
sections.content:
A URLAUTH component contains an access identifier, an authorization mechanism, and a token. The server computes the token from the URL and a secret mailbox access key. Each user has a separate key for each mailbox, and two users sharing a mailbox have different keys.

The key must be unpredictable and have at least 128 bits of entropy. The RFC defines the INTERNAL mechanism: the server chooses the algorithm and does not reveal the key. The token is represented as hexadecimal and is at least 128 bits long.
sections.plainLanguage: The server keeps a separate secret key for each user's mailbox. It uses that key to check whether a URL's authorization token is valid.

sections.title: Who May Use a URL
sections.content:
A URLAUTH component may be added only to an IMAP URL for a specific message or message part, and it must be at the end of the URL. It must not be used for a whole server, mailbox list, mailbox, or search result. An EXPIRE value can set the latest time the server accepts the URL.

The access identifier may limit use to a submission service acting for a named user, sessions logged in as a named user, any authorized user, or any session including anonymous ones. The latter two options offer less protection and should be used only for data that can be shared that broadly.
sections.plainLanguage: A URL can name a specific message or part and can set an expiry time. Its access rule can name one user, any signed-in user, a submission service, or anyone.

sections.title: Creating and Checking an Authorized URL
sections.content:
To create a URL, the server builds the URL through its access identifier, calculates a token with the chosen mechanism and secret key, and appends the mechanism and token. Hexadecimal avoids the padding character used by BASE64 that could complicate URL syntax.

To validate a URL, the server removes only the mechanism and token, identifies the mailbox, and recomputes the token. It must not decode percent escapes or change letter case. If the mailbox cannot be identified, the server still performs a token calculation with a plausible random key before rejecting the URL, to reduce timing clues about mailbox names.
sections.plainLanguage: The server checks a URL by recalculating its token. It uses a similar amount of work when a mailbox does not exist, so response timing reveals less about mailbox names.

sections.title: Resetting, Generating, and Fetching URLs
sections.content:
RESETKEY creates a new mailbox access key, invalidating URLs made with the old key. With no mailbox argument, it removes all keys for the user. GENURLAUTH asks the server to make authorized URLs and creates a key automatically the first time it is needed.

URLFETCH retrieves data for a valid URL even when the current session could not otherwise select that mailbox. The URLAUTH token does not grant more rights than the mailbox owner in the URL has at fetch time. Invalid URLs and URLs for whole mailboxes or servers return NIL.
sections.plainLanguage: GENURLAUTH creates an authorized link, and URLFETCH retrieves its data. RESETKEY changes the secret and makes earlier links made with that key stop working.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The mailbox key must be unpredictable. URLs using authuser or anonymous may be reused by a wider audience, so their content must be suitable for that audience. A server must protect mechanism details that could reveal sensitive information unless the session has confidentiality protection.

The server can delay repeated failed checks to limit computational denial-of-service attempts. It should also prevent a logged-in user from generating URLs under another user's identity unless that user is authorized to act for that identity or access its key table.
sections.plainLanguage: A URL is a credential, so anyone who obtains it may use the access it grants. Keep keys secret and choose an access rule that matches the sensitivity of the message.
